chunks.why: Wealthy, clever, adored; only gentle sorrow at Miss Taylor's marriage; takes up Harriet.
Manipulates Harriet away from Robert Martin toward Elton; her scheming feels effortless.
Harriet refuses Martin at Emma's prompt; Knightley angrily rebukes her, first real friction.
Elton's charade delights Emma; sister visits; reconciled with Knightley over the baby.
Christmas party goes well; but John Knightley warns Elton likes her, ignored; snow rising.
Elton proposes to HER in the carriage; humiliating rupture; Harriet's hopes destroyed by her folly.
Emma confesses blunder to Harriet; Elton engaged to Miss Hawkins; shame lingers.
Elton returns married; Harriet flutters; Frank Churchill arrives, promising distraction.
Frank charms; Emma and he gossip about Jane; Coles invite her; ball talk.
Cole's dinner: Emma made much of, dances with Frank, sings, back on top socially.
Ball planned then cancelled: Frank recalled by aunt; Emma imagines herself a little in love.
Mrs. Elton insufferable; Emma coolly dislikes her; Knightley denies Jane rumor, comfort.
Hartfield dinner strained by Mrs. Elton; Frank returning, nearby at Richmond.
Crown ball triumph: Knightley rescues Harriet from Elton snub, dances with Emma; gypsies incident.
Emma encourages Harriet toward Frank (as she thinks); Knightley suspicious; Donwell strawberries fine.
Box Hill: Emma insults Miss Bates; Knightley's stinging rebuke reduces her to tears; Jane taking governess post.
Frank-Jane secret engagement revealed; Harriet declares she loves Knightley; Emma realizes she does too. Nadir.
Knightley proposes and Emma accepts; Frank's contrite letter arrives; ecstatic reversal.
Plan for Knightley to move to Hartfield; Emma reconciles warmly with Jane; only Harriet clouds her joy.
Harriet engaged to Robert Martin (relief!); father consents; Emma marries Knightley. Perfect happiness.
